minutes.headline: Council on Aging heard facilities, sand-program and Fire Dept staffing updates; only minutes fix and adjournment voted.
minutes.summary: The Council on Aging opened with a facilities update (generator fence, flooring and rugs, kitchen, parking lot and playground design). Board comments covered a senior sand program, the FY26 COA budget presentation, and a call to support seven-day full-time Fire Department staffing. The only votes were a correction to the minutes and adjournment.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none was offered.

budget_items.topic: Capital plan: generator fence, flooring and rug replacement
budget_items.what_was_said: Fence is installed and will be stained when weather allows. Flooring and rugs depend on the town meeting vote on the capital plan.
A commercial kitchen is being completed for almost no money.
Running power for lights would need an electrician at a rough cost.
Money for parking lot design is in next year's capital plan if voted through; design could start in July.
The sand was funded by a grant to the fire department and the grant support continues.

budget_items.topic: COA FY26 budget and current-year accounts
budget_items.what_was_said: Two accounts were moved to office supplies and programs and approved.
The budget has no food line; participant payments fund the meals.
A speaker said the first-year increase would be large against the department's total budget, partly offset by ambulance receipts.

what_happened.line: The Council on Aging took no substantive votes; the only actions were a correction to the minutes and adjournment.
A speaker urged support for seven-day full-time Fire Department staffing, noting ambulance receipts would partly offset the first-year increase; no resolution was taken.
The Director is to meet the fire chief and town manager to plan a fall sand program, which a Fire Department grant funded and which continues.
Facilities update: the generator fence is installed, while flooring and rugs depend on the town meeting vote on the capital plan.
Two COA accounts were moved to office supplies and programs and approved as part of the FY26 budget discussion.

why_it_matters: Flooring and rugs, and the parking lot design, depend on a capital plan vote residents will be asked to take at town meeting.
The Fire Department staffing request would add a recurring cost to the town budget, and the speaker said ambulance receipts would only partly offset it in the first year.
watch_next: Town meeting vote on the capital plan, which governs the flooring, rugs and parking lot design (design could start in July if voted).
Fall sand program outreach planning, and any town manager response to the call for letters on Fire Department staffing.
